scope: Windows 11 development host, isolated desktop and generated folders; loopback model only.
before: Navigation past the session-cache limit erased unsent drafts or discarded a saved but unconfirmed plan. Manual saving being disabled did not protect an unsaved transcript.

checks: Two tabs with the same path keep distinct unsent drafts after 40 folder visits; no writes to settings or IPC for the drafts.
28 unfinished drafts survive 50 empty folder visits. Clearing the drafts restores the usual cache bound.
An actionable plan, manually unsaved text and a read-only session survive pressure; saved idle conversations later become reclaimable.
A simulated suspended timer cannot permit a late confirmation. The callback for an old plan cannot expire a new plan.

observations: Two file tabs for A stayed distinct. An unsent draft in the first A tab and a separate B draft were recovered; the pending plan came back only in the second A tab.
The saved A chat archive was byte-identical across navigation. No chat archive existed in B or in the 32 idle folders.
The output file was absent on return. Manual confirmation wrote the expected text only in A without a second model request.

verification.build: Verified 524 extracted source files against their SHA-256 inventory. Offline MSVC release build used a shared dependency/target cache. The exact resulting binary, all archived file hashes and the runtime manifest pin were verified.

limits: Drafts remain in memory, not on disk. Deliberate close of a following tab or application restart is outside the retention guarantee.
The expiry test used a controlled clock; native checks observed the actual host duration, not a 15-minute soak.
Frozen RC6 still requires clean Windows 10, clean Windows 11 and an authenticated provider turn.
